assessed_by: commit reading via GitHub API; no differential run

discovery.found_by: bbc_e2e mine-commits -> classify -> traversal; surfaced 2026-08-15 as the last open traversal-confirmed xstream row

the_candidate.message: Remove XStream dependency and related functionality
the_candidate.traversal: confirmed: direct bump 1.4.17 -> 1.4.18 in pom.xml @9506bd2e (2021-08-25), 186 commits before this commit

why_excluded.finding: The commit REMOVES xstream rather than adapting to it. There is no production code at the adaptation commit that uses the library, so a three-state differential is impossible in principle: the same driver cannot run at both the parent and the adaptation, because the classes it would drive no longer exist.
why_excluded.evidence: Every change is a deletion. pom.xml +0/-5 drops the dependency outright. FileQueryPropsReply.java (-84), FileQueryPropsRequest.java (-88), ContextImpl.java (-183) and InitialContextFactoryImpl.java (-44) are deleted files. ProtocolFactory -8, ProtocolVisitor -2, ProtocolVisitorAdapter -3, FiletransferImpl +1/-5, SecureClassLoaderObjectInputStream +1/-1. Three added lines across the whole commit, none of them an xstream call.
why_excluded.stated_motive: 'Eliminated the XStream library from the project, including all functionality utilizing it (e.g., JNDI filesystem, FileQueryProps). This reduces sec[urity surface]' -- the project's own commit body.
why_excluded.the_client_never_adapted: The dependency stood at 1.4.21 when it was deleted, and the boundary crossing to 1.4.18 happened on 2021-08-25. The project ran on post-boundary xstream for over four years and 186 commits without changing production code. Whatever the restrictive default cost them, it was not enough to force an adaptation -- which is itself a data point about how often this break bites.

why_the_miner_flagged_it.mechanism: Removal and adaptation look identical to the classifier. Both change production files that reference the library, both have commit messages naming it, and `is_production_adaptation` is true for both. The mined row even carried `version_at_commit: null` and `version_changed_here: false`, which in hindsight is the tell -- there is no version at the commit because the dependency is gone.
why_the_miner_flagged_it.screen_to_add: Reject a candidate whose diff NET-REMOVES the library dependency from the build file, or whose library-referencing production files are net-deleted. Cheap: it is visible in the pom patch and the per-file additions/deletions the classify step already fetches.
why_the_miner_flagged_it.second_tell: distance_commits was 186 and the gap between bump and 'adaptation' was over four years. A large distance does not disprove a case -- adaptations can lag -- but combined with a net-deletion diff it is conclusive.

consequence: xstream now has ZERO open traversal-confirmed candidates. Every one of its 10 has a case file: 6 verified_bbc, 2 signature_confirmed, 2 excluded.
